question: Why does the Cottonwood account-return function's explicit rewrite of 2026-07-27 read 3 rows (IB2 dry run under IRPT_DASHBD.TO-DB-b-329) when the carrier's holdings, transactions, realized and unrealized silver were full on that day? Read only; counts only; no id printed.
method: boto3 list and get on the function's own source table through the adapter's reader class (CottonwoodBlackDiamondSilverReader), table fact_allocations (ALLOWED_TABLES is fact_allocations and fact_transactions); the function derives a day from the allocations partitions of the day and the previous trading day and holds a day with no fact_transactions partition.
reading: The function's source for 2026-07-27 is fact_allocations, whose partition holds 3 accounts (full days hold about 880): the carrier is partial on that table for 2026-07-22 (157 accounts), 2026-07-27 (3), 2026-07-29 (1) and 2026-08-03 (159). 2026-08-19, 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-25 hold full allocations but have no fact_transactions partition, so the function holds them. All seven absent days are therefore carrier-side; the gold day 2026-07-27 cannot be rebuilt by the function until the carrier re-lands fact_allocations for it. The earlier read (RD_COT_CARRIER_ABSENT_DAYS_20261017.json) measured fact_holdings, a table this function does not read.
notes: Counts only. The signed pair for the 2026-07-27 rewrite (packet sha256 8596f43f) rested on the earlier read and is withdrawn by the issuer; nothing was written under it.
